graph.title: Arduino Zero MIDI Device (7 buttons + linear potentiometer)

parts.label: Arduino GND to top ground rail
top ground rail to bottom ground rail
bottom ground rail to pot GND

notes: The Arduino Zero is not in the catalogue, so the matched arduino-leonardo type is used. The Zero's IOREF pin (3.3 V on a Zero) is mapped to the Leonardo's 3.3V port.

The figure's breadboard has about 63 columns but the catalogue breadboard has 30. Columns were compressed and the order and connectivity kept. Each button spans columns 4i-3 to 4i-1, and its signal and ground wires go in the right-hand column (4i-1).
Bank 'b' (rows f-j) is the signal side of the button gap, next to the Arduino in the picture. Bank 't' (rows a-e) is the ground side.

Rail assignment follows the blue/red lines in the figure. The top rail row nearest the blue line is the ground rail (tn) and the row nearest the red line is the supply rail (tp). Likewise the bottom rail row nearest the blue line is bn.
The buttons use the internal pull-up (INPUT_PULLUP), so there is no external resistor. Each button's input side goes to its Arduino pin and the other side to ground.
The slide potentiometer sits off the breadboard. Its VCC, SIG and GND terminals are wired directly with jumper wires: supply rail to VCC, A0 to SIG, ground rail to GND.
The USB cable goes to the native USB port, which the catalogue USB cable type and Leonardo type do not name as ports, so the edge has no ports.

breadboard.name: Solderless breadboard
breadboard.port_rule: Holes are named '<column><bank>.<row>': column 1-30, bank 't' (top half, rows a-e) or 'b' (bottom half, rows f-j), e.g. '12t.c', '7b.h'. The 5 holes of one column-bank are one strip. Power rails: 'tp.<n>', 'tn.<n>', 'bp.<n>', 'bn.<n>' (each rail is one strip).

pushbutton.name: Pushbutton
pushbutton.note: 4 legs in two pairs: 1.l and 1.r are ALWAYS joined inside (side 1), 2.l and 2.r are ALWAYS joined (side 2); pressing joins side 1 to side 2. Wire the input pin to one side and the supply to the OTHER side; a pull-down/pull-up resistor goes on the SAME side as the input pin.
